study_title: Digital support systems to improve child development in Peru: A cluster-randomized controlled open label trial

gap_29_endline_surveys_vs_raw_gsed.finding: Exactly 29 participants completed the endline household survey (final_status == 1) with valid caregiver interview data, but their direct child GSED assessment was not administered or recorded. All 29 participants have missing el_gsed_dscore.

gap_20_published_exclusions_vs_actual_ex.finding: Actual exclusions in dataset and code are exactly 312 (307 missing raw GSED + 5 singleton age-band drops), yielding N=2,149 (2,461 - 312 = 2,149). If 332 were excluded, sample size would be 2,129, contradicting published Table 2 (N=2,149). The 20-case gap reflects an authorial drafting or calculation error in the manuscript footnote text.

mother_age.finding: Younger mothers have significantly higher outcome attrition (p < 0.0001).

low_birth_weight.finding: Low birth weight children (<2500g) have ~6.2 percentage points higher missingness (p = 0.028).

household_adults.finding: Households with more adults have lower outcome attrition (p = 0.018).

mar_mnar_feasibility_verdict.mcar_verdict: VIOLATED AND REFUTED: Missingness differs significantly by treatment arm (p < 0.001) and is strongly predicted by maternal age, birth weight, and household size.
mar_mnar_feasibility_verdict.mar_verdict: FEASIBLE WITH LIMITATIONS: 71.5% of outcome attriters have full baseline data intact, and another 20.8% are missing only father variables or MICS. Multiple imputation for the full cohort (N=2,461) is technically feasible under MAR, but MAR is inherently unprovable and cannot account for unobserved disengagement or child mortality.
mar_mnar_feasibility_verdict.mnar_verdict: STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: A tipping-point / delta-adjustment sensitivity analysis varying unobserved outcome offsets across arms is essential to stress-test treatment efficacy.
